html:
SMTO-SKL-0166 — SMTO couldn't get an answer from GitHub

GUID: 50110e93-e579-5fe7-bae2-881b139ad957
Slug: github-provider-unavailable
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • GitHub didn't reply in time, had a server problem, or gave an unexpected answer. If you asked for a change, SMTO can't be sure whether it happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure this computer is online and that github.com opens in your browser. The page githubstatus.com shows whether GitHub has an outage. SMTO can only finish the request when GitHub is reachable and working.
  2. If you asked for a change, such as a comment, a new issue or a merge, open it on github.com and check whether it already happened. GitHub may have made the change even though SMTO didn't get the reply.
  3. Repeat your request. Only repeat a change if you confirmed it didn't happen. Looking things up again is safe, but repeating a change could do it twice.

What success looks like

  • Your request completes, or you can see on github.com that the change is already there.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat a change on GitHub until you've checked it didn't already happen.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The GitHub request hit the invocation deadline, failed after the read retry on transport or server errors, or received a status classified as provider_unavailable.

What this means

  • GitHub reaches a deadline, exhausts read transport/server recovery or returns another status classified as provider unavailable. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • GitHub reaches a deadline, exhausts read transport/server recovery or returns another status classified as provider unavailable.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect actual status, deadline or transport failure rather than asserting a global outage.

How to fix it

  • GitHubClient raises provider_unavailable on the 180-second invocation deadline, after one retried read transport/5xx failure, or for an unmapped HTTP status. Check GitHub status and network connectivity, then retry a read; for a write, inspect the exact object on GitHub before deciding to repeat it.
  • Check GitHub availability and connectivity, then retry a read. Inspect receipt certainty before attempting any write again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A later bounded read succeeds, with any earlier uncertain write reconciled separately.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
